title: input_request.created
description: An agent needs something from the human before continuing. Parity with flowpilot's input_requests + EventKind.INPUT_REQUESTED: a question and an approval are the same animal, and the kind field is the only difference.

job_id.description: The job left waiting for the answer.

session_id.description: The session that asked. Optional because the path of the answer outlives the session: it emits the request and the process ends.

node_id.description: The node the job was on when it asked (t167). Stamped by the server from the owning job, never coming from the request body — the same trust boundary as job_id. NULL means "it is not known which node it came from": a job with no position, or a request recorded before the field existed.

kind.description: question: somebody needs to know something. approval: a manual gate wants an OK on an artefact.

context.description: Evidence, the alternatives weighed, what has already been tried.

oneOf.description: One short label for one decision — the shape this list has always had, and the shape a single-decision escalation keeps forever.
One control of a batched question: a whole step's worth of decisions asked at once, answered as one JSON document keyed by each field's id.

id.description: The key this field's value carries in the answer document.

label.description: What the person reads beside the control.

kind.description: choice: pick one. multi: pick any number. free_text: type it.

options.description: What there is to pick from, for a choice or a multi.

recommended.description: What the agent would pick for this field. The union of these, across the fields that state one, is what default_answer carries — derived, never hand-written.

options.description: The decisions being asked for: short labels for one decision, or an ordered list of fields when a whole step is asked at once.

recommendation.description: What the agent would choose, in the imperative.

default_answer.description: The value auto-approval applies on the human's behalf.

auto_approvable.description: Whether the auto-approval gate MAY answer in the human's place. Carried explicitly: "no options and no default" was never a good proxy for unapprovable.
